judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade 3 (rank 3, resolved coordinates) Skills under the Listening and Speaking (Oral) Skill Area: the first is Term 2, Sub-strand 'Daily / Weekly activities in all areas of Language and other subjects' ('With support, predicts what will happen in a story, e.g., "Look at the title and the cover of the book. What do you think is going to happen?"'); the second is Term 4, Sub-strand 'Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities' ('Discusses solutions to a problem using higher order thinking skills, e.g., "If your father can't collect you this afternoon you could..."'). They share meaningful, pair-specific instructional coherence as complementary Grade 3 oral higher-order thinking behaviours: each requires the learner to reason aloud about what might happen or what could be done in a situation that is not yet determined, and the Learning Components tag both as oral with prediction vs problem-solving/higher order thinking emphases. This is substantive reinforcement rather than generic repeated CAPS wording. It does not, however, support buildsTowards in either direction: the two statements address different objects (story events cued by title/cover vs a real-life contingency), sit under different sub-strands, and show no deepening of the same capability (no more text, more independence on the same task, or broadened scope of the same behaviour); the nomination signals are non-semantic (Grade-only shared ancestor, rank gap 0 flagged 'weak', single shared LC tag 'oral', stopword-level token/trigram overlap). Material limitations: both endpoints omit 24 source-evidence items and are flagged truncated, and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so the full printed source wording is unavailable; relatesTo is the defensible symmetric judgment on the bounded evidence.

They share the same grade coordinate (Grade R, rank 0), the same Skill Area (Emergent Writing) and Sub-strand (Handwriting), and LC tags overlap on emergent writing/handwriting/motor, so there is genuine perceptual-motor coherence underpinning handwriting readiness. However, they address distinct motor domains (midline crossing/gross motor versus hand-muscle fine motor strengthening) that CAPS lists as parallel readiness activities; the Term 1 to Term 2 placement alone does not show that proficiency in midline crossing substantively supports success in fine-motor hand-strengthening, so a directional buildsTowards is not warranted. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R, Listening and Speaking (Oral), Sub-strand 'Uses language to think and reason' (resolved coordinate rank 0 for both). The second SFI is printed in the Term 2 table ('Matches things that go together, and compares things that are different'; LCs 'Matches things that go together' and 'Compares things that are different', tags matching/comparing/reasoning), while the first is in the Term 4 table ('Classifies things according to own criteria and more complex criteria such as textures'; LC tags classifying/criteria/reasoning). This is not mere repeated wording: matching and comparing similarities/differences is the earlier Term 2 capability, and Term 4 extends it to grouping by the learner's own and more complex criteria such as texture, so proficiency in matching/comparing supports success in criterion-based classification. Direction is therefore second_to_first (Term 2 to the later Term 4 within the same grade), which is the only permitted intra-grade developmental direction here. Evidence limits: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), the second endpoint's supporting LC metadata is truncated, and several ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context (merged Grade R and Term banners), so Term placement rests on the identity_scope values shown.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Writing under a Handwriting/Emergent Handwriting sub-strand, so direction must follow Term order. The second SFI is Grade R Term 2 ('Copies patterns onto pegboards and copies patterns, words and letters onto paper'), and the first is Grade R Term 4 ('...creating drawings, making more complex patterns with crayons' alongside catching play). This is not mere repeated wording: the Term 2 work is guided copying of given patterns, words and letters, while the Term 4 statement moves to independently generating drawings and explicitly 'more complex patterns' with crayons, an expansion from reproduction to self-produced, more demanding pattern formation supported by the same fine-motor/pattern LCs (copying patterns, patterns with crayons, creates drawings). Control gained in Term 2 pattern copying plausibly supports success with the Term 4 more complex pattern-making, so buildsTowards runs Term 2 (second) to Term 4 (first). Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the Term 4 statement also bundles a gross-motor catching component not developmentally dependent on the Term 2 copying, which tempers confidence.

Direction is Term 1 to Term 2 within Grade 1, which is the permitted forward order. Endpoint source evidence is truncated and both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context, but the retained statement text and identity scopes are unambiguous.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade 2 (rank 2) Reading and Phonics. The second SFI is Grade 2 Term 3, Sub-strand 'Daily Phonic Activities' ('Recognises vowel digraphs and diphthongs such as ‘oy’, ‘oi’, ‘ay’, ‘ai’'); the first is Grade 2 Term 4, Sub-strand 'Group Guided Reading' ('Monitors self when reading, both word recognition and comprehension'). Direction is therefore constrained to the earlier Term 3 statement toward the later Term 4 statement. Substantively, secure recognition of vowel digraph/diphthong spelling patterns supplies the decoding knowledge a reader draws on to recognise words accurately, which is explicitly one of the two components ('word recognition') the Term 4 statement requires learners to monitor and self-check during connected reading; so proficiency in the phonics skill supports likely success in self-monitoring while reading. The link is supportive rather than a strict prerequisite (self-monitoring also involves comprehension), and endpoint source evidence and the first SFI's LC evidence are truncated, so confidence is moderate; the shared Grade ancestor and token overlap ('and') alone were not treated as evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit under Grade 3 (rank 3) of the same CAPS framework but in different Term scopes: the first is Grade 3 / Term 3 / Writing / Shared, Group and Independent Writing ('Identifies and uses nouns, pronouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs and prepositions correctly'), the second is Grade 3 / Term 4 / Listening and Speaking (Oral) / Daily-Weekly activities ('Uses terms such as subject, verb, object, question, statement, command, synonym, antonym, exclamation mark when discussing texts'). Direction is from the earlier Term 3 statement to the later Term 4 statement, which is permitted within a grade. The change is substantive rather than repeated wording: the first establishes identification and correct use of word classes (LC tags 'grammar', 'parts of speech', 'word classes'), while the second extends this into metalanguage used orally to discuss texts, adding sentence-function and sentence-role terms (subject, object, question, statement, command) and semantic terms (synonym, antonym) (LC tags 'metalanguage', 'language terms', 'discussing texts'). Secure command of parts of speech such as verbs plausibly supports success in naming and applying these grammatical terms when talking about texts, so buildsTowards first_to_second is supported. Evidence limitation: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, so judgment rests on the bounded statement text, LCs and resolved Grade/Term scopes supplied.

Term 2 to Term 4 within Grade 3 would be a permitted direction, but the pair-specific change is a shift of domain rather than demonstrated expanded capability, so symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit at the same canonical coordinate (Grade 1, rank 1) and under the same Term 1 banner, but in different Skill Areas and Sub-strands: 'Listens to and discusses stories and other texts read aloud' is a Reading and Phonics / Emergent reading skills statement (shared and guided reading comprehension and oral response), while 'Listens without interrupting' is a Listening and Speaking (Oral) / daily-weekly activities statement about attentive, turn-taking listening behaviour. They share the 'listening' LC tag and the token 'listens', and are substantively coherent as complementary oral-listening behaviours that both operate in whole-class listening settings, so meaningful reinforcement exists. However, the evidence shows no substantive expansion in scope, independence, or complexity in either direction within the same Grade and same Term that would justify a developmental dependency; attentive-listening conduct and listening-to-and-discussing-texts are parallel Term 1 expectations rather than one clearly supporting success in the other. judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit under Grade 3 (rank 3) but in different terms and skill areas: the second is Grade 3 / Term 2 / Writing / Shared, Group and Independent Writing ('Identifies and uses nouns, adjectives, verbs and adverbs correctly', LCs tagged grammar, nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, usage), and the first is Grade 3 / Term 4 / Listening and Speaking (Oral) / Daily-Weekly activities ('Uses terms such as subject, verb, object, question, statement, command, synonym, antonym, exclamation mark when discussing texts', LC tagged grammar, language terms, metalanguage). Direction is therefore constrained to the earlier Term 2 statement toward the later Term 4 statement. Substantively, secure identification and correct use of word classes (including verbs) in writing supports the later, broader metalinguistic demand of naming sentence functions (subject, verb, object), sentence types (question, statement, command) and word-meaning relations (synonym, antonym) while discussing texts orally, so proficiency in the Term 2 skill plausibly supports success in the Term 4 skill. This is an inferred curriculum-grounded relation rather than an established prerequisite; the lexical overlap alone ('uses', 'verb') was not treated as sufficient, and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each), which limits confirmation beyond the supplied statements and ancestry.

A Term 4 to Term 3 direction would also be invalid within one grade. Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment; source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits any stronger progression claim.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3 Skills but sit in different Skill Areas and sub-strands: the first is 'Reads own and others' writing' (Term 2, Reading and Phonics / Paired-Independent Reading), the second is 'Writes short words in the joined script or cursive writing' (Term 1, Writing / Handwriting). The nomination signal is essentially one shared token, 'writing', used in two different senses (written product vs. script formation), so the lexical overlap alone carries no developmental weight. There is, however, genuine pair-specific coherence: the text children read in the paired/independent reading activity is their own and their peers' handwritten writing, so legible joined-script production and reading of own/peer writing are complementary parts of the same classroom reading-writing cycle. Handwriting fluency is not evidenced here as a dependency for decoding or comprehending peer texts (which rests on phonics and reading practice), so a developmental Term 1 to Term 2 buildsTowards claim is not substantively supported; symmetric relatesTo is the appropriate judgment. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence (and truncated LC evidence for the first SFI), so the full source wording is only partially visible, which limits confidence but does not contradict this reading.

They are complementary audience-directed independent writing tasks - a short functional/procedural text for a known reader and illustrated topic sentences produced for a shared class book - so there is genuine, pair-specific instructional coherence beyond generic repetition. However, the bounded evidence shows a change of text type and purpose rather than a substantive extension of capability (no evidence of longer texts, greater independence, or greater complexity in the Term 3 item relative to the Term 1 item), and the nomination signals are only shared ancestry, the broad 'writing' tag, and stopword/trigram overlap ('a', 'to', 'writes'). That does not meet the bar for buildsTowards in this deliberately repetitive CAPS framework, so the symmetric relatesTo with null direction is the correct complete judgment. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so this judgment rests on the supplied statement text, term/sub-strand placement and Learning Components only.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade 1 Reading and Phonics (rank 1). The second SFI is Term 1, Sub-strand 'Emergent reading skills', and explicitly develops basic concepts of print including 'Concept of book - cover, front, back, title' (confirmed by its Learning Component 'Develops the concept of book - cover, front, back, title'). The first SFI is Term 3, Sub-strand 'Shared Reading', 'Uses cover of book to predict ending and storyline' (LC: 'Uses the cover of a book to predict the ending and storyline'). This is not mere repeated wording: the later statement applies the earlier print-concept knowledge of what a book cover is to a more demanding comprehension task (making predictions about ending and storyline), so proficiency with the Term 1 book/print concepts supports success with the Term 3 cover-based prediction. Direction is Term 1 to Term 3 within Grade 1, which is a permitted earlier-to-later direction. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, but the quoted statement texts and identity scopes are sufficient and non-contradictory for this judgment.

The demand expressed in the statement, its LC text and its LC tags is unchanged, so the bounded evidence shows CAPS re-stating the same emergent picture-'reading'/storytelling capability rather than extending it; the differing Skill Area and sub-strand heading are hierarchy and lesson-context labels, which alone cannot establish developmental dependency. buildsTowards is therefore not supported despite the admissible lower-to-higher grade direction. The recurrence is nevertheless pair-specific and instructionally coherent — the Grade R emergent 'reading' of pictures is deliberately carried into the formal Grade 1 reading programme and practised within Shared and Group Guided Reading — so this is meaningful reinforcement without dependency, i.e. canonical relatesTo with null direction and unchanged canonical endpoint order. Confidence is moderate because both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the LC metadata excerpt is truncated, and because all listed SFIs carry upstream audit/merge context that was not independently resolvable.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 3, Term 1, Skill Area WRITING, but under different printed sub-strands: 'Draws pictures and writes sentences to show understanding of a story' belongs to Shared, Group and Independent Writing (composition/comprehension-response), while 'Spaces words correctly in lines' belongs to Handwriting (letter/word formation and spacing conventions). Their LCs confirm distinct capabilities (writing/drawing to show story understanding vs handwriting spacing on lines). They are complementary aspects of producing written text in the same term and coherently reinforce each other (legible, well-spaced script supports readable sentence writing), but the evidence does not establish that proficiency in one materially raises likelihood of success in the other, and both are same-Grade/same-Term so no directional sequence is supported. The trigram overlap ('ces') and shared page 113 are incidental, not semantic. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and all nodes carry upstream merge/audit context, so judgment rests on the bounded statement text, sub-strand placement and LCs.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in the identical Grade 1 / Term 3 / Reading and Phonics / Group Guided Reading context (same table row, same page), so there is no grade or term offset to supply developmental direction. Substantively they are complementary components of the same guided reading practice: reading aloud from one's own book in the teacher-led group, and continuing to build sight vocabulary from the incidental reading programme, graded reading series and high-frequency word lists. The relationship is reciprocal rather than dependent — growing sight vocabulary eases oral reading, while reading aloud from the graded series is itself a vehicle for acquiring sight words — and the shared evidence is mostly generic ('reading', 'a', 'the', shared ancestors, page proximity), which is insufficient to assert a same-rank developmental direction in either orientation. Meaningful conceptual coherence within one sub-strand supports relatesTo. Source and LC evidence for both endpoints is flagged truncated, which limits but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Second SFI is Grade R (rank 0), Term 4, Emergent Reading / Shared Reading: 'Points at words rather than pictures when reading' (LC tags: emergent reading, pointing, print awareness, words). First SFI is Grade 1 (rank 1), Term 4, Reading and Phonics / Group Guided Reading: 'Shows an understanding of punctuation when reading aloud' (LC tags: fluency, punctuation, reading aloud). Both are shared/guided oral-reading skills centred on attending to printed text rather than illustrations; the Grade R learner's concepts-about-print behaviour (tracking and attending to the actual words during reading) is the earlier capability that supports the Grade 1 extension of attending to finer print conventions (punctuation marks) and letting them shape phrasing when reading aloud. This is substantive extension from word-level print awareness to sentence-level punctuation/fluency, not mere repeated wording; direction is the permitted lower-to-higher grade (Grade R to Grade 1). Note that the nomination signals themselves are weak (shared tokens 'reading'/'when' only) and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), so confidence is moderate.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade 3, Term 3, Skill Area WRITING, Sub-strand 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' bullets from the same source page/table row. 'Uses a variety of vocabulary to make the writing more interesting' concerns word choice during composing; 'Reads own writing to the class' concerns sharing/presenting a completed own text aloud. They are complementary stages of the same independent writing cycle (compose, then share own text with an audience), which gives substantive coherence, but the evidence shows no expanded capability or dependency in either direction: neither varied vocabulary nor reading aloud is presented as a precondition for the other, and they sit at identical Grade/Term coordinates (rank 3, Term 3), so same-rank directional evidence is absent. Shared LC token 'writing' and page proximity are weak nomination signals only. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so absence of further linking text is not proof; the supported conservative judgment is symmetric relatesTo.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are the identical printed CAPS Skill bullet 'Sequences pictures of a story' in the Listening and Speaking (Oral) skill area, but at different resolved grade coordinates: the first at Grade R (rank 0), Term 3, under the sub-strand 'Daily activities in all areas of Language and other subjects', and the second at Grade 1 (rank 1), Term 2, under 'Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities'. The cross-grade direction is lower-to-higher (Grade R to Grade 1), which is the only permitted developmental direction here. The recurrence is not merely generic wording: the Grade R occurrence sits in incidental daily ring activities for emergent oral work, while the Grade 1 occurrence sits in timetabled, twice-weekly focussed listening and speaking lessons, indicating the same picture-sequencing comprehension skill applied in a more formal and demanding oral-comprehension context. Emergent competence in orally sequencing story pictures in Grade R therefore plausibly supports success with the Grade 1 requirement; the shared Learning Component 8708c5ec confirms a single underlying skill rather than two unrelated statements. Evidence limitation: source-evidence and LC excerpts for both endpoints are truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each), so the full printed task context for each grade is not visible, which keeps confidence moderate rather than high.
